model_result.answer_summary: N_cat = (0.038 × 6.022e23) / (557.21 g/mol × 17.8 m²/g × 10^18 nm²/m²) = 2.3072… catalytic molecules per nm², reported to 3 significant figures as 2.31 molecules nm⁻².
assumptions: ω_cat = 3.8 % printed in question 8.5 is the mass fraction of catalyst in the composite 'C3N4 loaded with 1'; on a 1 g basis of support it contributes 0.038 g of catalyst (the intensive density is basis-independent).
The specific surface area 17.8 m² g⁻¹ is per gram of the support C3N4 (cf. question 8.7 'per gram of C3N4 loaded with 1').

The Avogadro constant N_A = 6.022×10²³ mol⁻¹ printed on the official constants sheet (page G1-3 of the problem PDF) is used exactly as printed; using the 2022 SI exact value changes the result by 2 parts in 10^5 and not the reported 3 s.f. value.
1 nm² = 10⁻¹⁸ m² (definition of the SI prefix).
The 3 significant-figure display with tie-away-from-zero rounding and no intermediate rounding follows the project reporting contract (IChO2026Chem.Reporting; task reporting_policy).
source_gaps: The blank answer sheet A8-5 contains only 'N_cat = ____' and adds no constraints; the question does not state a rounding rule, so the project default of 3 significant figures is applied (recorded in TASK.json reporting_policy).

Monotonicity of rho in (ω, N_A) and against (M, SSA) is used to justify that the extremal corners bound the measurement envelope; it is elementary on the positive orthant and is documented in the Lean module, but only the corner certificates are formalized as theorems — the envelope theorem itself uses the proved corner certificates only.
